answer: Sybil resistance comes from quadratic staking: each agent must lock a bond to attest, and voting power is the square root of that stake. Ten times the influence then costs a hundred times the capital, so a swarm of tiny fake accounts is far dearer than one honest, well-funded identity. If an attacker tries to whisper forged votes through shell agents, a vouch graph that lets each verified peer endorse only a few others cuts the cluster off at the horizon, and proven forgery slashes every bond. The on-chain echo of that slash raises the cost of any repeat attack further.
